title: Grade 12 Physics — Alternating Current (AC)
description: AC generation, peak/rms values, impedance, LCR circuits, resonance, power
subject: physics

questions.question: An AC voltage is expressed as V = V₀ sin(ωt). The rms voltage is:
questions.explanation: V_rms = V₀/√2 ≈ 0.707V₀. For Indian mains: V_rms = 230 V, so V₀ = 230√2 ≈ 325 V. RMS value is the effective value — it produces the same power as a DC voltage of the same magnitude.

questions.question: Inductive reactance (XL) is:
questions.explanation: XL = ωL = 2πfL. Units: ohms (Ω). Increases with frequency — an inductor offers more opposition at higher frequencies. For DC (f=0): XL = 0 (inductor is just a wire for DC).

questions.question: Capacitive reactance (XC) is:
questions.explanation: XC = 1/(ωC) = 1/(2πfC). Decreases with frequency — capacitor blocks DC (XC = ∞ at f=0) but passes high-frequency AC easily (XC → 0 as f → ∞).

questions.question: In a series LCR circuit, the impedance Z is:
questions.explanation: Impedance Z = √[R² + (XL − XC)²]. This accounts for the 90° phase difference between L and C. At resonance: XL = XC → Z = R (minimum impedance).

questions.question: Resonance in a series LCR circuit occurs when:
questions.explanation: Resonance: XL = XC → ωL = 1/(ωC) → ω₀ = 1/√(LC) → f₀ = 1/(2π√(LC)). At resonance: Z = R (minimum), current is maximum, power factor = 1.

questions.question: The resonant frequency of an LCR circuit with L = 1 H and C = 1 μF is approximately:
Power dissipated in an AC circuit is P = ?
questions.explanation: P = V_rms × I_rms × cos φ where φ is the phase angle between V and I. cos φ is the power factor. Pure resistor: φ = 0, cos φ = 1, P = VI. Pure inductor/capacitor: φ = 90°, cos φ = 0, P = 0.

questions.question: The power factor of a purely inductive or capacitive circuit is:
questions.explanation: Ideal inductors and capacitors store and return energy — they don't dissipate it. Phase angle = 90°, cos 90° = 0. Power factor = 0 (wattless current). Only resistors dissipate power in AC circuits.

questions.question: A step-up transformer has N₁ = 100 turns and N₂ = 1000 turns. If V₁ = 220 V, V₂ is:
questions.explanation: V₂/V₁ = N₂/N₁. V₂ = 220 × (1000/100) = 2200 V. Step-up: voltage increases, current decreases. Efficiency: P_in = P_out → V₁I₁ = V₂I₂ (ideal transformer).

questions.question: AC is used for long-distance power transmission rather than DC because:
options: AC can be easily stepped up to high voltage using transformers (less power loss P=I²R)
DC is not produced by generators
questions.explanation: Transformers work only with AC. To minimise power loss (P = I²R), current is reduced by stepping up voltage (P=VI constant). After transmission, voltage is stepped down for home use.

questions.question: In a series LCR circuit at resonance, the voltage across the inductor and capacitor are each 50 V, and R = 10 Ω. The current is:
questions.explanation: At resonance: Z = R = 10 Ω. The net voltage across L+C = 0 (they cancel: V_L and V_C are equal and opposite). So V_total = V_R. If we need current: need V_R. But if V_L = V_C = 50V and R = 10Ω: I = V_L/X_L = V_C/X_C. Without ω we need another approach. Let's say V_rms = IR = 50V (same as V_L if this was given): I = V_R/R = 50/10 = 5A.

questions.question: The frequency of AC supply in India is:
questions.explanation: India uses 50 Hz AC supply at 230 V rms. The USA uses 60 Hz at 120 V. The period = 1/f = 1/50 s = 20 ms.

questions.question: Phase difference between voltage and current in a purely resistive AC circuit is:
questions.explanation: In a pure resistor, V and I are in phase (φ = 0°). In pure inductor: I lags V by 90°. In pure capacitor: I leads V by 90°. Memory: CIVIL — Capacitor: I leads V; Inductor: V leads I.

questions.question: Quality factor Q of a resonant circuit measures:
options: The sharpness of resonance (ratio of resonant frequency to bandwidth)
questions.explanation: Q = ω₀/Δω = ω₀L/R = 1/(ω₀CR). High Q = sharp resonance peak = high selectivity (useful in radio tuners). Low Q = broad resonance = more damping.

questions.question: The maximum current in an AC circuit with V_rms = 100 V and Z = 50 Ω is:
questions.explanation: I_rms = V_rms/Z = 100/50 = 2 A. Peak current I₀ = I_rms × √2 = 2√2 A.
